summary: A satirical, humorous article about a wellness workshop series run by the Local Center for Emotional Enlightenment (LCEE), titled "Tender Loving Care or TLC—For Those Who Can't Even Keep a Cactus Alive." Starting September 3, 2023, weekly sessions led by comically named experts cover communication, insecurities, love languages, modern dating, accountability, co-dependency, commitment, kindness, love potions, and relationship breakups. The piece compares tending a love life to caring for a houseplant.
one_line: A satirical write-up of the LCEE's weekly relationship workshop series running from September 3 to November 19, 2023, likening love to houseplant care.
key_facts: The Local Center for Emotional Enlightenment (LCEE) began hosting the workshop series "Tender Loving Care or TLC—For Those Who Can't Even Keep a Cactus Alive" on September 3, 2023.
Attendees Jane Dough and Tom Foolery joined the first workshop with a dozen other romantically challenged participants; Tom Foolery was allegedly ghosted by a literal ghost.
Paula Bond, a relationship guru whose cat has more Instagram followers than most reality stars, led the opening session.
On September 10th, Sarah Nade, who has a Ph.D. in obvious things we all ignore, taught that relationships die from silence and partners must actually talk.
On September 17th, couples therapist Dr. Ophelia Payne taught attendees to confront insecurities without the silent treatment or passive-aggressive social media comments.
On September 24th, Dr. Hugh Morris led the "Speak My Language, Not Gibberish" workshop on the five love languages, noting not everyone appreciates sarcasm as an expression of love.
On October 1st, Luna Tick guided the dating session "Swipe Right For Romance—or Just Order Takeout."
On October 8th, Dr. Blamey led "It's Not You, It's Definitely Me," about accountability.
On October 15th, Polly Anna led "Perfect is Boring, Be Better-ish Instead," urging attendees to be someone's Prince or Princess Charming-ish.
On October 22nd, Captain Obvious taught about co-dependency, saying "Don't be a barnacle."
On October 29th, Madame Enigmatica led a group séance on commitment fears, concluding that spirits fear vows less than the living.
Early November's "Open Hearts, Not Just Doors" was led by Dr. Kindly Gentler, who argued chivalry isn't dead, just snoozing.
On November 12th, Chef Délectable led "Brewing Romance or Disaster?" on love potions and cooking your way into someone's heart.
On November 19th, Dr. Grave Concern led the closing "Thriller Night" workshop, in which participants re-enacted break-ups and make-ups as zombies and mummies.
